ex-sci10-01-q04.a: A balanced chemical equation has an equal number of atoms of each element on both the reactant and product sides (e.g., 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O). Hence they are opposites.

ex-sci10-04-q05.a: (a) Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH): Methyl carbon forms 3 single bonds with H and 1 single bond with carboxyl carbon; carboxyl carbon forms a double bond (=O, 2 shared pairs) with one O (having 2 lone pairs) and a single bond with –OH oxygen (having 2 lone pairs and 1 single bond to H). (d) F₂: Each F atom (7 valence e⁻) shares 1 electron pair to form F–F, with 3 lone pairs on each F atom.

Both possess huge numbers, vast surface area and dense capillary networks.

ex-sci10-08-q04.q: How is the sex of the child determined in human beings?
ex-sci10-08-q04.a: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes: 22 autosome pairs and 1 pair of sex chromosomes — XX in females and XY in males. All eggs carry an X chromosome, while half the sperms carry X and half carry Y. If an X-bearing sperm fertilises the egg, the zygote is XX (girl); if a Y-bearing sperm fertilises the egg, the zygote is XY (boy). Thus sex is determined by the chromosome inherited from the father (50:50 chance).

ex-sci10-11-q18.q: Explain the following: (a) Why is the tungsten used almost exclusively for filament of electric lamps? (b) Why are the conductors of electric heating devices, such as bread-toasters and electric irons, made of an alloy rather than a pure metal? (c) Why is the series arrangement not used for domestic circuits? (d) How does the resistance of a wire vary with its area of cross-section? (e) Why are copper and aluminium wires usually employed for electricity transmission?
ex-sci10-11-q18.a: (a) Tungsten has an extremely high melting point (3380 °C) and high resistivity, so it glows white-hot without melting. (b) Alloys have higher resistivity than pure constituent metals and do not oxidise (burn) readily at high temperatures. (c) In series, if one appliance fails the entire circuit breaks, appliances cannot be switched independently, each gets reduced voltage, and high- and low-power devices cannot draw their required currents. (d) Resistance is inversely proportional to area of cross-section (R ∝ 1/A): thicker wires have lower resistance. (e) Copper and aluminium have very low electrical resistivity (minimising I²R heat loss) and are ductile and economical.

ex-sci10-12-q09.q: What is the function of an earth wire? Why is it necessary to earth metallic appliances?
ex-sci10-12-q09.a: The earth wire (green insulation, connected to a metal plate deep in the ground) provides a low-resistance conducting path for leakage current. Earthing metallic-bodied appliances ensures that if live wire touches the metal casing, its potential remains equal to earth potential and leakage current flows safely to ground, protecting the user from severe electric shock.

No, organisms of any trophic level cannot be completely removed without damaging the ecosystem because all trophic levels are interdependent.

ex-sci10-13-q06.q: What is biological magnification? Will the levels of this magnification be different at different levels of the ecosystem?
ex-sci10-13-q06.a: Biological magnification (biomagnification) is the progressive increase in concentration of non-biodegradable toxic chemicals (such as DDT, pesticides, heavy metals) at successive trophic levels of a food chain. Yes, levels increase up the food chain and are highest at the top trophic level (e.g., human beings and predatory birds).

ex-sci10-13-q09.q: Why is damage to the ozone layer a cause for concern? What steps are being taken to limit this damage?
ex-sci10-13-q09.a: The stratospheric ozone layer (O₃) shields life on Earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which causes skin cancer, cataracts, immune damage and harm to crops/plankton. Steps taken: Under UNEP’s 1987 Montreal Protocol, nations froze CFC production at 1986 levels and mandated CFC-free refrigerators, ACs and aerosols.
